scope: Proposition C.2 (Typical-state gradient dissipation) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 122. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 ≤ β < 1/2. There are constants c > 0 and C < ∞, and events of disorder probability tending to one, on which a set BJ ⊆ {−1, 1}n satisfies µJ (BJ ) ≤ e−cn and, for every f0, every t ≥ 0, and every configuration x, (∂t − L)U(Stf0)(x) ≤ [−c + C1BJ (x)] U(Stf0)(x). (C.8) The constants depend only on the fixed β. If 0 ≤ β ≤ 7/20, the exceptional set can be empty.
